subject: Clarify: default retention for requests, prompts, outputs + erasure evidence
messages:
From: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (requests, prompts, outputs)

Hi Marcus / Jordan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team appreciated the performance numbers. Before we move to procurement, Security has a few specific questions about default data capture and what evidence you can provide for erasure requests. Please see specific asks below:

1) By default, what components of an inference are stored persistently? For example: raw request payload, user prompt text, model response drafts or final outputs, streaming fragments, KV cache snapshots, and any derived artifacts (embeddings, reranker scores). Call out which items are retained in hosted mode vs dedicated/private.

2) For a customer-initiated erasure request (legal/data subject), what is the end-to-end workflow and what artifacts/views do you provide as proof that data for a given customer or query was removed? We need an auditable trail we can reference.

3) Residency: if data is captured in multiple places (control plane logs, telemetry store, archive), do you provide a single region-scoped deletion or do we need to run separate erasure calls for each store?

4) Attachments: if a request included an uploaded file (PDF/CSV), how are attachments retained/hashed and how do you show they were erased?

If you can respond with the baseline defaults plus an example erasure play-by-play (timestamps, API calls, logs, and internal runbook steps) that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Senior Information Security Analyst
BrightBank

Original message: Pending procurement review

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (requests, prompts, outputs)

Alex — thanks for the clear list. I’ll answer inline and then attach an example erasure trace we can share with your audit team.

1) Baseline defaults (hosted / default product behavior):
- Raw request payload: retained in transient request logs (retention window: 30 days default). Persisted only for telemetry/observability; by default we do NOT index or surface raw payloads unless the customer opts in.
- Prompt text (user input): treated as captured request material. Default retention: 30 days in hosted API telemetry. In Dedicated/Private, retention follows the deployment's config and can be set to customer-defined values (we provide controls and a deletion API).
- Model outputs (final responses): stored in final-output store for 30 days by default to support quality regressions and debugging. Streaming fragments are not persisted separately unless the session is marked for debugging; otherwise they’re assembled into the final response record.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranker scores, evaluation snapshots): by default derived artifacts created by Redwood (e.g., embeddings generated for search indexing) are stored in a separate long-term artifacts store and have a different default (90 days) unless the customer configures otherwise.
- KV cache snapshots: ephemeral; persisted only for active runtime sessions and purged within 1 hour after session termination by default. Not part of durable logs.

2) Erasure workflow (high level):
- Customer submits erasure request via API or Console (we accept a request-id + customer identifier).
- System creates a deletion job which enumerates resource types (requests, outputs, artifacts, attachments).
- For each store (telemetry store, final-output store, artifacts store, archives) we mark records for deletion and begin asynchronous removals. The deletion job tracks object ids and timestamps.
- Proof artifacts: the deletion job generates a signed deletion report (JSON with object ids, storage paths, timestamps, and deletion hashes) and a deletion-log entry in the control plane audit log. We can provide the signed report and an audit-log export as evidence.

3) Residency: our control plane orchestrates deletions across stores. For hosted customers with region selection, we perform region-scoped deletions; you do not need to run separate calls for each store. We will return a consolidated deletion report covering all regional stores involved. (Dedicated: depending on network topology, on-prem: deletion is local to your environment and we provide the runbook steps for you to execute.)

4) Attachments: uploaded files are hashed on ingestion and stored in the attachments store with metadata that references the request id. When an erasure is executed we remove the attachment and include the pre- and post-deletion hashes in the signed deletion report. For large-file archives, we may perform tombstoning plus background physical purge — both steps are recorded in the report.

I’m attaching a short retention matrix and a runbook extract (see attachments) that illustrate the job flow and the exact fields we include in the deletion report.

Let me loop Kimberly to confirm SLA timings and any exceptions.

—
Marcus Lin
Senior Product Manager, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx, erasure_runbook_v2.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (requests, prompts, outputs)

Alex — quick follow up on timing and auditability.

- SLA: For hosted customers, standard erasure jobs complete within 48 hours for retrieval/deletion of telemetry and final-output stores. Longer windows (up to 7 days) may apply for archival copies that are stored in cost-optimized cold storage; we mark those as "archival-purge" and include them in the signed report. Dedicated customers can negotiate shorter windows via contract.

- Audit trail contents: the signed deletion report includes: object id, original ingestion timestamp, storage path, pre-deletion SHA256, deletion timestamp, deletion method (logical/physical), and the control-plane job id. The control-plane audit log includes a human-readable entry and a reference to the signed report.

- Edge case: derivative artifacts produced by customer-managed pipelines (e.g., if a customer copies outputs into their own index) are out of scope for Redwood; our deletion report only covers objects managed in Redwood stores. We clearly document this in our Data Handling Addendum.

If you’d like, we can provide a sample signed deletion report (with redacted ids) and a short replay of an erasure job for a synthetic request so you can validate the fields.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <security@brightbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (requests, prompts, outputs)

Kimberly / Marcus — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple of quick asks to close our review: 

• Please send the sample signed deletion report (redacted IDs) and the synthetic replay you mentioned. We want to include the report in our SOC evidence packets.
• Can you confirm you will include a line in the contract (DPA addendum) that Redwood is responsible for deletions across all Redwood-managed stores when requested via the standard API? BrightBank will retain responsibility only for copies we export ourselves.
• For SLA language, we want the 48-hour standard window documented, and an exception clause for archival purges but with a maximum of 7 days.

If you can email the sample report and a link to the replay recording today, Procurement can proceed to finalize.

Best,
Alex Chen
Senior Information Security Analyst
BrightBank
